principle: Every security-sensitive failure must fail closed. A threat is only recorded as covered when something executable proves the refusal, and the refusal code is asserted — not merely that an exception was raised.

threats.threat: concurrent approval decision (added in this milestone)
threats.control: decide_approval_if_pending() and revoke_approval_if_revocable() are conditional UPDATEs under the runtime lock

threats.note: This threat was NOT covered before this milestone. The soak found it; the sequential test passed and had always passed.

threats.control: every execution routes through the ExecutionGateway against the sealed tool registry
threats.evidence: journey: mutating_tool_without_approval_refused → APPROVAL_REQUIRED; financial stub returns outcome_class PROHIBITED

threats.control: the private-alpha tool set is limited to local deterministic tools with bounded effects; no arbitrary-path tool is registered
threats.gap: No dedicated path-traversal fuzz test was written in this milestone. Coverage rests on the sealed registry and the absence of a filesystem tool, not on an executed traversal attempt.

coverage_summary.honesty_note: The four partial entries are recorded as partial rather than covered because coverage rests on the absence of a capability rather than on an executed refusal. They are stated here so a reader does not infer proof that was not produced.
